title: Diary for Kids: Free Online Diary, Ideas and Tips
description: A free diary for kids to write in online, plus how to write a diary for kids, what to look for in a paper diary, 50 fun ideas and simple tips for parents.
h1: Diary for kids: write, learn and have fun
intro: A diary for kids is a private place where children write or draw about their day, their feelings and the things they love. You can start right now with the free diary below, no sign up needed, or use this page to choose a paper diary and find fun ideas to write about.

sections.h2: How to write a diary for kids

blocks.p: Writing a diary is easy. Here is how to do it, one step at a time.

steps.name: Write the date
steps.text: Put today's date at the top, like Monday, May 4. Now you will always know when it happened.

steps.name: Say hello
steps.text: Write **Dear diary,** like you are talking to a friend. You can even give your diary a name.

steps.name: Tell what happened
steps.text: Write about one thing you did today. Who was there? Where were you?

steps.name: Say how you felt
steps.text: Happy, silly, sad, excited, brave? Write why you felt that way.

steps.name: Add a drawing
steps.text: If you are writing on paper, draw a small picture of your day. Pictures count too.

steps.name: Say goodbye
steps.text: End with goodnight, see you tomorrow, or your name.

example.label: A kid's diary
example.title: Dear diary,
example.text:
Today we baked cookies with Grandma.
I cracked the eggs all by myself.
One egg fell on the floor and the dog ate it!
The cookies were warm and gooey.
I felt proud and happy.
Goodnight, Leo

blocks.tip: Kids who are just learning to write can draw a picture and write one sentence. That is a real diary entry.

sections.h2: Our free online diary for kids

blocks.p: The diary at the top of this page is free and simple. Kids type, and their page saves by itself in the browser on that device. There is no sign up, no account and no email.

ul: **Private.** Pages stay on your device. They are not posted anywhere or sent to us.
**PIN lock.** A PIN keeps the diary closed on a shared family computer. It is a simple lock, not encryption.
**Print it.** Print any page or save it as a PDF to keep in a folder.
**Works anywhere.** Use it in any browser on a computer, tablet or phone. There is no app to download, but you can add it to the home screen.

blocks.p: Pages are saved on one device only and do not sync, so if a child writes on the family tablet, the pages stay on that tablet. Open the full [online diary](/) any time.

blocks.p: Find many more on our pages of [journal prompts for kids](/journal-prompts-for-kids/) and [diary entry topics](/diary-entry-topics/).

ul: **Respect privacy.** Kids write more honestly when they trust that their diary will not be read without asking. Agree on this as a family.
**Keep it short.** Five minutes at bedtime is plenty. Small and often builds the habit.
**Write together at first.** Younger kids can tell you their day while you write it, then add their own drawing.
**Do not correct spelling.** A diary is not homework. Let them enjoy writing.
**Model it.** Kids copy what they see. Keep your own diary or journal.
**Make it fun.** Stickers, colored pens and a special pencil case make diary time feel like a treat.
**Stay safe online.** Remind kids not to share diary pages or personal details online.

blocks.p: For school writing, the [diary entry format](/diary-entry-format/) page shows the layout teachers expect, with a simple version for younger children.

sections.h2: Why a diary is good for kids

blocks.p: A diary gives kids a quiet place that is all theirs. It is practice for reading and writing without the pressure of a grade. It helps them name their feelings, which can make big feelings easier to handle. And it becomes a lovely record of childhood that they can read when they are older.
Faith families might also like our ideas for a [prayer journal for kids](/prayer-journal-for-kids/).

faq.q: What age should a child start a diary?
faq.a: Many children start around 6 to 8 years old, once they can write a few sentences. Younger kids can keep a picture diary, drawing their day and saying one sentence for a grown up to write down. There is no wrong age to begin.

faq.q: What should kids write in a diary?
faq.a: Kids can write about what they did today, what made them happy or sad, their friends, their family, their favorite things, and things they imagine. Drawings, lists and short stories all count. Prompts like What was the best part of today help when they get stuck.

faq.q: How do you write a diary for kids?
faq.a: Write the date, then Dear diary. Tell one thing that happened today and how it made you feel. Add a drawing if you like, and end with goodnight or your name. Keep it short and fun. A few sentences is a great diary entry.

faq.q: Is this online diary safe for kids?
faq.a: Our online diary has no sign up, no account and no sharing. Pages are saved only in the browser on that device and are not sent to us. A PIN can keep it closed on a shared computer. Parents should still talk with kids about keeping personal details offline.

faq.q: What is a good diary to buy for a child?
faq.a: Look for wide lines, some blank space for drawing, undated pages, thick paper and a sturdy cover. A lock and key makes it feel special for ages 7 to 12. Diaries with a short prompt on each page help children who do not know what to write.
